body:
@AThousandShips 

Hi AThousandShips, thanks for tagging my PR! I'm a first time code contributor to the Godot project and I'm excited to participate :)

I've submitted 4 bug fixes for the profiler graph — mainly around preserving spikes and valleys when zooming, fixing unnecessary redraws at zoom limits, fixing panning for touch pads, and resetting zoom state when the profiler is cleared. All my code changes are in 1 file, and are approximately 2 to 20 lines long.

Could you explain the process to me? Do I just wait for someone to review my PRs or is there anything I should do to help move things along? I imagine reviewers are really busy — do you have a rough idea of how long reviews typically take?

Thanks for your time I appreciate it!

Nothing specific is needed, relevant maintainers have been assigned for review and will review this when able, for the general process, please see [here](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/pull_requests/pr_workflow.html)
Did yo profile (heh) how these changes affect _editor_ performance?

I'm not sure I can help you with performance profiling, don't know much about it. I just noticed the extra do-while and for loops and thought that might make the `_update_plot()` function more expensive.
Feel free to ask for advice in rocketchat - https://chat.godotengine.org/
There's some info about engine profiling in official docs - https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/engine_details/development/profiling/index.html#using-c-profilers

Hey @arkology  and @AThousandShips  - good news - I enhanced the fix for the Profiler Graph not displaying performance spikes and it now executes FASTER than the released code. So we get the fix and we get better performance - win win :)

I updated the description for the PR - check it out for the timing details.
Hey @uoslider-wq, are you using AI to generate the code, or are you writing it yourself?

Hi @Ivorforce , nice to meet you :)

I appreciate your question! I've been using the Godot engine to create a game so I've been using the Godot profiler quite a bit. It has a bunch of issues that hinder getting the result developers want. 

So I've submitted 6 PRs to fix things in the profiler graph area. So folks (including me) can get the most out of it:

This PR here is a serious issue I discovered while using the profiler on my game - that the graph would hide and flicker the performance spikes - which was very unhelpful. I've used C++ quite a bit in my software development career so I felt comfortable diving in. 

I asked the AI to give me a detailed description of the drawing method. Then looking at the code with that knowledge it was easy to see that the sampling frequency was skipping over the performance spikes. Knowing that it was simple to add code to gather the data between the sampling windows and compress it to one value for the plot points. 

However this approach added time to the drawing loop because now you have the additional loop I added (the do while). @arkology pointed this out to me as a possible performance issue. I really wanted to fix this graph so I decided that I'd try to optimize by combining 2 loops into one and pre-collect the data outside the drawing loop. This was important because the hashmap lookup was in both the 2 loops and it's an expensive CPU call. All through this process I used the AI as a sounding board for my different ideas. Talking with it about combining loops, what are the expensive CPU calls, what variable initializations would be good to bring outside the loop, where the bottlenecks were, etc. 

I probably did 3 iterations on trying to optimize and combine the loops using my own code, snippets of AI code, and all the while making changes and tweaks. Then I did testing to make sure it worked, then added timing statements to see any improvements in speed. I was very excited to see that the speed was better even than the code out in the field! Along this cycle I gave the code to the AI to run a double check for bugs and issues. It pointed out a few things, and I decided what was important and made those changes. 

This PR is the first one I ever submitted anywhere for an open source project :)

I should also mention my PR #117382 .It's about a performance optimization for the drawing code for the profiler graph. It's a 2 line fix that improves the graph drawing speed 4X! I would never have found this issue without the AI. I asked it to look for optimization possibilities in the drawing code specifically and it pointed out the pass by reference vs value issue and how expensive the implicit deep copy was. Using that information I put in timing code to get before times, fixed the 2 lines, and ran it again to get the after fix times. I put those times in the PR so check them out.

That's how I use the AI as a software developer.
I hope that helps answer your seemingly simple - but actually complex question.

Thanks for the detailed description. It sounds like a sensible way to use AI. Please note however that we require contributors to [disclose the use of AI](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/pull_requests/pull_request_guidelines.html#ai-assisted-contributions) in the PR description.
Please amend your PR descriptions accordingly, and review the [PR rules](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/pull_requests/pull_request_guidelines.html) to make sure to abide by them in the future.

No worries, i'll amend my PR descriptions and take a look at the links you
sent 👍

Hi @Ivorforce , @AThousandShips , @arkology ,

I completely changed the code to fix the "Profiler: Fix for graph not displaying performance spikes at different zoom levels" PR #117066. I also updated the PR description and uploaded new movies of the before and after fix behavior.

My new code is very targeted and it's the minimal code change to fix the issue. As such it's a much simpler change and should be vastly easier to review. My previous code included lots of performance optimizations and restructuring. I think it was too much change for a single PR.

I'm new here so I'm still figuring out the process and what the best way is to submit code fixes that move easily through the system. If you have a moment take a glance at the code and let me know if it's more compatible with the review procedure, or if there is anything I could do or change to make that easier. I'm also available to do a code walk through on any of my PRs (see below) if that would be helpful for reviewers.

All the PRs I've submitted are focused on the profiler #117200, #117120, #117084, #117083.
Including one accepted and merged #117382.
